title: Grace window for reserved pool overconsumption with automated invoice adjustments
creator: Arielle Gomez
description: Problem: Customers on Reserved capacity occasionally experience short burst overages (1-10 minutes) due to traffic spikes or canary rollouts. Current behavior immediately marks overage and generates rate-limit throttles and billing events, which creates noisy incidents and downstream charge disputes. Goal: introduce a configurable grace window that will allow transient overconsumption to continue serving for a bounded time while we 1) accumulate fine-grained telemetry, 2) automatically compute invoice adjustments for post-hoc billing reconciliation, and 3) surface a billing signal in the Console so customers can opt-in/out. The feature must be safe (no silent bill surprises), auditable, and reversible.

decisions: Default grace-window duration: 5 minutes (configurable per-tenant up to 15 minutes).
Behavior during window: allow serving at reserved pool rate but mark tokens as 'grace_overage' in ledger for later billing adjustments.
Billing treatment: auto-draft an invoice adjustment entry that appears on next invoice as 'Reserved capacity transient overage (grace)' with link to ledger rows and audit trail.
Fail-safe: hard throttle at tenant-level if overage persists beyond configured maximum (15 minutes).
Visibility: Console shows a live banner, historical table, and cost preview for affected billing period.

acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-tenant grace window exists and default is disabled for non-enterprise tenants.
During grace window the quota service allows requests to be served and emits 'grace_overage' ledger rows with tenant id, start/end, token counts and metadata.
Invoice adjustments are auto-generated (draft state) and visible in Console billing preview and in the customer's invoice timeline.
All actions are logged and auditable with links from Console to ledger rows and raw request traces.
E2E load test: simulated spike for 100 tenants shows no increase in customer-facing 429s, and reconciliation job matches ledger totals to invoices within tolerance (<0.1%).
